newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A phone-tapping row has flared at Government House following the discovery of recordings and documents implicating the Democrat secretary-general in vote-buying. Sanan Kachornprasart has dismissed the recordings and documents as a fabrication and insisted he has never bought votes. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Constitution Drafting Assembly's (CDA) first draft charter is set to undergo minute scrutiny in the next few weeks by key political institutions, which have reservations over various controversial points. CDA president Uthai Pimchaichon will hear the opinions of Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh at a meeting on Friday, while the House of Representatives and the Senate are planning separate sessions to discuss the draft. (THE NATION)

- Vientiane has called for harsh action against men accused of raping four Lao girls in a police cell in Rayong province. The call was made in a letter handed yesterday by Sithong Jityothing, charge d'affaires of the Lao Embassy, to Abhorn Manasvanich, director general of the East Asian Affairs Department. (BANGKOK POST)

- A massive plan to resuscitate the troubled property market is approved by the Cabinet. The Cabinet has approved extraordinary and unique measures to deal with the problem, which has been blamed for the problems in the banking and financial sectors as well as the parlous state of the Stock Exchange of Thailand. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The state should hold no more than 30 percent in a proposed national maritime fleet with the private sector taking the rest, a committee says. The permanent secretary for Transport and Communications says the proposal will be submitted next month to the Office of the Maritime Promotion Commission and then passes on to the Cabinet. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thai garment exporters, who last year shipped out 79 billion baht worth of products, have lowered their projection for 1997 to 90 billion baht from 101 billion baht on weaker-than-expected demand for low-priced items. The president of Thai Garment Association says exports are expected to be 10 percent below the government's target of 101.07 billion baht, totalling about 90 billion baht. (THE NATION)
